claims.claim: Usage is collapsing: NEAR's daily active accounts and transactions are far below a year ago.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Averages may mask short‑term spikes or off‑chain activity.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Averages can be distorted by measurement changes or one-off activity, but both the 30-day and 90-day comparisons point the same way.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
A 30-day mean could be distorted by a single anomalous week, though the 90-day window (w90.active.yoy_pct, w90.txns.yoy_pct) confirms the same trend.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The decline may reflect a shift to less frequent but higher-value usage, not necessarily a collapse in real activity.

claims.claim: The remaining usage is worth more: fees and transfer value per active account have risen, so the drop in accounts overstates the drop in real economic activity.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Per‑active metrics are derived indirectly; total economic activity could still be lower.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Per-account averages can rise because low-value or automated accounts left, and total gas fees still fell.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Higher per-account value could reflect a few large Intents users rather than broad-based economic intensity among remaining accounts.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Higher fees per user could be due to price inflation rather than increased economic value per transaction.

claims.claim: Account counts were inflated: the drop in new accounts and active contracts since the 2024 peak points to automated or incentive-driven activity that has since left.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Decline could reflect a market cycle rather than prior incentive‑driven inflation.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
The data show the decline but cannot prove it was automated or incentive-driven rather than genuine user attrition.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
The dramatic drops in new accounts and active contracts are real, but the data cannot directly distinguish automated or incentive-driven activity from genuine organic churn.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The drop in new accounts and contracts may reflect a maturation of the ecosystem rather than exit of incentive-driven actors.

claims.claim: Value moving on NEAR is growing: USD transfer volume is well above a year ago.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Volume increase is partly driven by price appreciation.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
USD volume can be inflated by price appreciation and large transfers, so it is not a clean measure of organic activity.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
USD volume is a function of both token quantity and price; if price falls, this growth reverses without any change in real transfer activity.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The rise in USD volume may be driven by price appreciation rather than increased real economic activity.

claims.claim: Gas fees do not pay for security: annual gas fees are tiny next to the value of new token issuance.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Issuance includes supply growth, not all of which is inflationary.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
The comparison values issuance at current price and does not measure actual security spend.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Gas fees are not the only mechanism that could fund security; app-level revenue or buybacks could in principle be redirected, though the data shows they currently are not.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The chain may still be secure if issuance is used for long-term incentives or network growth, not just inflation.

claims.claim: Measured against gas fees, the valuation is far ahead of usage: market cap is thousands of times annual gas fees.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Market cap reflects future expectations, not just current security costs.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Gas fees exclude app and Intents revenue, so the ratio may overstate overvaluation if value accrues elsewhere.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
If app fees rather than gas fees are the correct denominator, the ratio drops to under 80x (valuation.mcap_to_app_fees), which is far less extreme.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Market cap could be justified if future growth in app fees or Intents revenue is expected.

claims.claim: Activity is not a leading indicator of price on NEAR: changes in active accounts barely predict the next quarter's price.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Correlation measured over a limited period; other lag structures may exist.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
A weak historical correlation does not rule out predictive power at other horizons or in nonlinear relationships.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Low correlation does not rule out a non-linear or lagged relationship that this specific Pearson test over a 3-month horizon would miss.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Low correlation may reflect noise or structural changes in how price is driven, not a lack of predictive power.

claims.claim: Supply inflation is modest: total supply grew only a few percent in the last year.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Even modest inflation can erode value if demand doesn’t keep pace.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Supply growth can change and does not account for buybacks or burns outside the total supply series.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
A low percentage growth rate on a large supply base still produces over $100M in new token value (fees.issuance_usd_365d), which matters for dilution.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Modest supply growth may not be sustainable if future issuance increases or demand remains weak.

claims.claim: Most of the growth in dollar transfer volume is the price rise: counted in NEAR tokens, transfer volume is only slightly above a year ago.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Share calculations are based on means and may not capture all dynamics.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
The decomposition uses 30-day means and may be sensitive to outliers or price measurement.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
The decomposition uses log-shares that do not sum to exactly one, so the attribution is approximate rather than exact.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The share of growth from price may be misleading if NEAR's utility is increasing despite low volume in NEAR terms.

claims.claim: Real usage moved to cross-chain swaps: NEAR Intents fees are well above a year ago, while account counts fell.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Intents represent only one type of activity; overall usage may still be declining.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Intents fee growth may reflect fee mix or pricing, and sampled swap USD volume actually fell.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Intents fee growth could be driven by a temporary surge in cross-chain arbitrage rather than durable user adoption.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Growth in Intents fees may be temporary or driven by a single protocol, not broad ecosystem adoption.

claims.claim: Gas fees are the wrong yardstick: users pay the apps on NEAR many times more than they pay the chain, and that total is growing.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
App fees include many services; a high ratio doesn’t imply security is cheap.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
App fees are concentrated in Intents and may not accrue to NEAR holders.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
App fees are gross user charges, not all of which accrue to NEAR token holders; only the kept share (intents_daily.kept_share_30d) flows back.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The app fee growth may be concentrated in a few protocols, not representative of overall user spending.

claims.claim: Holders now get paid: the NEAR Intents revenue that NEAR keeps is used to buy back the token, and it is several times higher than a year ago.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Revenue may not be fully used for buybacks or may not translate to price support.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
The buyback program is recent and small relative to market cap and issuance, so 'get paid' may overstate holder cash flow.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
The buyback program only started in February 2026 (holders.days = 260), so the year-ago comparison for revenue reflects a period before buybacks existed, making the growth partly mechanical.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Buybacks may be unsustainable if revenue growth slows or token price drops.

claims.claim: It is a one-product economy: almost all app fees on NEAR come from NEAR Intents, and few other apps earn meaningful fees.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
A small number of other apps could grow rapidly in the future.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Fee share does not capture non-fee economic activity or apps with revenue outside fees.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Four protocols over $100/day is a snapshot; new apps could be emerging that have not yet crossed that threshold but may diversify the ecosystem soon.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The dominance of Intents may be due to a recent launch or marketing push, not long-term ecosystem health.

claims.claim: Even counting buybacks, holders are still diluted and the price is rich: buybacks cover only a minority of new issuance, and market cap is hundreds of times that revenue.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Future revenue growth could improve coverage and lower valuation multiples.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Buyback coverage uses annualised recent revenue and issuance value at current price, both of which can change.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
If Intents revenue continues its 334% YoY growth trajectory, coverage of issuance could rise rapidly and the valuation multiple could compress quickly.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Holders may still benefit if buybacks are reinvested or if future revenue grows faster than issuance.

claims.claim: The numbers can be trusted: a second, independent provider reports the same gas fees as the first.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Only gas‑fee data were cross‑checked; other metrics may still differ between providers.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Agreement on gas fees and price does not validate all other metrics or their methodology.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Agreement on gas fees and price does not guarantee agreement on active-account or transaction counts, which come from only one provider.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Cross-checks may not catch systematic biases in data collection or reporting delays.

claims.claim: NEAR is already deflationary: buybacks and burned fees outweigh new issuance.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Burned fees are not quantified; they could offset issuance but are not shown here.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Total supply may already net some burns, but the provided series shows growth rather than deflation.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
If burned fees or other mechanisms not captured in these metrics exist, the net inflation picture could differ, but no such data is provided here.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Data on burned fees and buybacks is not available to confirm net supply change.

claims.claim: NEAR is a ghost chain: almost nobody pays to use anything on it.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
While on‑chain gas fees are low, app fees indicate users do pay for services.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Activity is far below peak and concentrated in Intents, so 'ghost chain' may be rhetorical rather than literal.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
While fees are meaningful in aggregate, they are concentrated in a single product and a small user base, so 'ghost chain' is wrong on revenue but partially right on breadth.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Low chain fees may reflect high app-level fees, not lack of usage, if users are paying apps instead of gas.

claims.claim: Stablecoin liquidity on NEAR is growing alongside NEAR Intents.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Stablecoin metrics may lag or be measured differently across sources.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Stablecoin averages can be affected by a few large holders or migrations, but the provided trend is negative.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
Stablecoin supply could lag Intents growth if users route through cross-chain swaps without parking stablecoins on NEAR, so the contradiction may narrow in coming months.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Growth in stablecoin volume may be due to speculative activity rather than real DeFi usage.

claims.claim: DeFi on NEAR is shrinking: value locked and exchange volume are below a year ago.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
TVL and DEX volume are increasing, though other DeFi metrics could be declining.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
TVL and DEX volume can be price-inflated, and stablecoin liquidity is down.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
TVL and DEX volume grew, but stablecoin liquidity shrank (stables.yoy_pct), so the DeFi ecosystem is shifting in composition even if it is not uniformly shrinking.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
Tvl and dex volume may be inflated by synthetic assets or leveraged positions.

claims.claim: Daily transactions on NEAR are higher than a year ago.
caveats: gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight)
Daily transaction counts are averaged; occasional peaks may exist but are not reflected in the mean.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek)
Transaction counts can be affected by batching or spam changes, but the measured trend is lower.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu)
This is a control claim and is clearly false; the only way it could be true is if a different transaction definition were used, but the provided data is unambiguous.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba)
The claim may be true if it refers to a different metric (e.g. total transactions including non-user activity), but daily user txns are down.

gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight).thesis: The data show a stark collapse in active accounts and transaction volume on NEAR, while the modest supply growth and high market‑cap multiples indicate that valuation is far outpacing genuine on‑chain usage; the ecosystem is heavily reliant on a single product (Intents) and app fees dwarf gas fees, suggesting limited sustainable demand.
gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI, open-weight).would_change_my_mind: If 30‑day average daily active accounts and transaction counts both rose by more than 50% year‑over‑year while gas‑fee revenue and app‑fee revenue remained low, indicating a genuine resurgence of core usage.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek).thesis: The evidence supports a bearish long-term case for NEAR as a general-purpose chain: core active accounts, transactions, new accounts, and active contracts have collapsed, gas fees are tiny versus issuance, and market cap is extremely high relative to gas fees. The main offset is NEAR Intents, where app fees and retained revenue are growing and buybacks have started, but that activity is concentrated, stablecoin liquidity is shrinking, and buybacks cover only a minority of issuance.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek).would_change_my_mind: A sustained multi-month increase in active accounts and transactions alongside broadening app-fee growth beyond NEAR Intents and stablecoin liquidity growth.

GLM-5.2 (Zhipu).thesis: NEAR's core on-chain usage has collapsed—active accounts and transactions are down 78–85% year-over-year and 97% from peak—yet the surviving activity is far more economically valuable per account, driven almost entirely by NEAR Intents, which generates growing fees (up 51% YoY), revenue (up 334% YoY), and token buybacks. The bull case rests on Intents becoming a durable cross-chain revenue engine, but the chain is a one-product economy (87% of app fees from Intents, only four protocols over $100/day), buybacks cover only a fifth of new issuance, and the market cap is hundreds of times annualized Intents revenue, making the setup fragile and richly valued.
GLM-5.2 (Zhipu).would_change_my_mind: A sustained six-month recovery in monthly active accounts back above 200,000 (monthly.2025-11.active level) combined with apps.intents_share_30d falling below 0.50, indicating diversified organic adoption rather than single-product dependence.

Qwen3-30B (Alibaba).thesis: NEAR's ecosystem is undergoing a structural shift: user activity has declined sharply, but economic value per user has increased, driven by NEAR Intents and app fees. The chain is becoming more efficient and valuable per transaction, with growing app-level revenue and buybacks, though it remains highly dependent on a single product and faces challenges in sustaining growth amid low on-chain usage and modest supply inflation.
Qwen3-30B (Alibaba).would_change_my_mind: If daily active accounts and transaction volume show sustained growth over the next 6 months, while app fees and Intents revenue continue to rise, it would indicate a recovery in organic user adoption.
